operations.rationale: Replace the plan-node lifecycle-state table with reader prose while preserving the canonical AI/research state matrix. October 11 reconciliation keeps current-grant reuse, node-local holds, job/effect separation, qualified reuse, unknown outcomes and observed recovery aligned with the canonical owner.
content_lines: Plan states describe eligibility for a particular node. Proposed work is not execution authority. Missing context, an incomplete dependency, or an undefined verifier may hold that node while separately authorized review or independent work proceeds.

A missing valid grant differs from an unavailable credential. Resolve applicable existing authority before asking for a new owner decision; an approval cannot by itself repair a credential. A dispatchable node may request a typed job, but job dispatch does not establish an attempted or observed external effect. Runtime still checks its own current admission conditions.

Replanning records changed assumptions and the affected future uses. Preserve completed work only while its dependencies, coverage and acceptance criteria remain eligible. Current-use decisions can change without erasing permitted historical records. Changes outside the accepted envelope need re-contract; allowed choices can continue under a current valid grant.

Stop and recovery claims need observations appropriate to their scope and accountable residual owners. A timeout after a remote request may leave an unknown effect; a new plan cannot turn it into no effect or silently make a blind retry safe. Completion requires the downstream observations and acceptance receipts appropriate to this obligation.
